headline: Caregivers need breaks too
subhead: That's what respite care is for.
changes: Respite care is short-term care for your parent so you can rest, run errands, work or travel.
It can be a few hours or a few days: an aide at home, an adult day program, or a short stay in a care facility.
NJ's Statewide Respite Care Program helps eligible families with respite costs.
It has financial eligibility rules. Your county office can tell you whether your family qualifies.
verdict_text: Taking a break isn't giving up. Rested caregivers give better care, and stay caregivers longer.
actions: Ask about the Statewide Respite Care Program
Save this for when you need it

headline: What 20 hours a week of home care costs in NJ
subhead: A starting point for planning.
changes: About $38 an hour: the 2025 statewide median for home health aide care in New Jersey (CareScout).
20 hours a week ≈ $3,293 a month ($38 × 20 hours × 52 weeks ÷ 12). Rates vary by county and agency.
Medicare usually won't pay for ongoing help with daily activities like bathing and dressing.
Medicaid, VA benefits or long-term care insurance may help, depending on eligibility.
verdict_text: Knowing the rough cost early helps families plan, and ask about help paying before savings run low.
actions: Ask what you may qualify for: 877-222-3737

headline: Holidays when a parent has dementia
subhead: Small changes can make the season easier for everyone.
changes: Keep the routine: usual mealtimes and bedtimes, and visits at your parent's best time of day.
Smaller is better: fewer guests, less noise, shorter visits, and a quiet room they can go to.
Prepare guests ahead of time. Suggest they introduce themselves and keep conversation simple.
Include them with a familiar, simple job: folding napkins, stirring, or looking at old photos together.
verdict_text: New faces, noise and changed routines can be overwhelming for someone living with dementia. A few adjustments help them, and help you.
actions: Share this with family before the visit

headline: Hiring home care for a parent? Ask these first.
subhead: A good agency will be glad you asked.
changes: Are you registered with NJ Consumer Affairs? Every agency that places aides in NJ homes must be.
Are your aides certified home health aides (CHHA) in New Jersey, and do you verify it with the Board of Nursing?
Are aides your employees or contractors? It affects who pays taxes and carries insurance.
Who supervises care? NJ agencies must have a licensed health care supervisor, such as a registered nurse.
What happens if the aide can't come? Ask about backup coverage, minimum hours and changing aides.
verdict_text: Bringing someone into your parent's home is a big decision. Checking registration first protects your parent and gives you somewhere to turn if something goes wrong.
actions: Get costs and cancellation terms in writing

headline: Facility Check: choosing a North Jersey nursing home?
subhead: Three public records to check first.
changes: Care Compare star ratings: Medicare.gov/care-compare rates every Medicare- and Medicaid-certified nursing home on inspections, staffing and quality. Look at each rating, not just the overall stars.
Inspection reports: on the same page, open the inspection results. Look for deficiencies marked as harm or "immediate jeopardy," and problems that repeat year after year.
The Special Focus Facility list: CMS publishes a monthly list of nursing homes with a history of serious quality problems, plus candidates that qualify but haven't been selected.
Then visit more than once, including a mealtime or evening. Watch how staff talk with residents and how quickly call lights are answered.
verdict_text: If something's wrong after move-in, the NJ Long-Term Care Ombudsman investigates concerns for residents 60+. Complaints are confidential, and anonymous complaints are accepted. In an emergency, call 911.
actions: Each month we'll check the CMS list for North Jersey

headline: Last day: Medicare open enrollment ends today
subhead: Changes take effect January 1, 2027.
changes: Today is the last day to change Medicare health or drug plans for 2027.
Check that your parent's prescriptions, doctors and pharmacy are still covered next year.
verdict_text: If your parent's current plan still fits, they don't need to do anything. If not, today is the day to switch.

headline: County Compass: Bergen County
subhead: Caring for an older adult in Bergen? Here's your first call.
changes: Bergen County Division of Senior Services: Senior HelpLine 201-336-7400. One Bergen County Plaza, 2nd floor, Hackensack.
Its Information & Assistance / Care Management unit is Bergen's Aging & Disability Resource Connection (ADRC), for older adults, caregivers and adults 18+ with a disability.
Ask about care management, Ride Connect transportation, and 10 county-run senior activity centers, each with a meal program.
Before you call, have your parent's town, age, what's getting harder (meals, rides, bathing, bills) and their insurance.
verdict_text: You don't need to have it all figured out. Calling and asking "where do I start?" is exactly what this office is for.
actions: Not in Bergen? Call 877-222-3737 for your county ADRC

headline: Your parent's 2027 Medicare and Social Security numbers
subhead: Both changes are final and start in January.
changes: Social Security benefits rise 3.6% in January 2027. The average retirement benefit goes up about $75 a month.
The standard Medicare Part B premium rises to $209.40 a month, up $6.50 from $202.90.
The Part B deductible rises to $292 (from $283). The Part A hospital deductible is $1,776 per benefit period.
If your parent has a my Social Security account, the 2027 COLA notice is already in the Message Center. Paper notices arrive by mail in December.
verdict_text: Part B usually comes out of the Social Security check, so the raise your parent actually sees will be a little smaller than 3.6%. Higher-income beneficiaries pay more for Part B.
actions: Check the new amount in my Social Security
Paper COLA notices arrive by mail in December

headline: Scams against older adults: the new FTC numbers
subhead: What the report found, and a simple plan to make with your parent.
changes: Adults 60+ reported about $3 billion in fraud losses in 2025. The FTC estimates the true cost may be far higher.
People 80 and older who lost money reported a median loss of $2,000.
Older adults were more likely to report losing money to tech-support, prize and government-impersonation scams.
Warning signs: urgency, secrecy, and payment by gift card, wire, crypto or cash handed to a courier.
verdict_text: Hang up and call back on a number you already trust: the one on the card, statement or official website. Never use a number from the message itself.
actions: Agree on a family code word
Ask your parent to call you before sending money

headline: Recall: Xentrawave adult bed rails
subhead: A person can get trapped in or beside the rail. One death has been reported.
changes: Model XT016, all batches, and model XT026, batch 20251212 only. Model number is on the box and manual.
Black or gray metal frame, gray foam grips, gray fabric pouch with a green "Xentrawave" label.
Sold on Amazon.com, May 2025 through August 2026, for about $37 to $40. About 2,114 sold.
For any portable bed rail: check for gaps between the rail and mattress, and keep the retention strap attached.
verdict_text: Stop using a recalled rail now and contact Xentrawave for a full refund. You'll be asked to cut the foam grips and send a photo.
actions: Look up any bed rail brand at cpsc.gov/recalls
Ask a doctor or OT if a rail is right for your parent

headline: One week left to change Medicare plans for 2027
subhead: Open enrollment ends Monday, December 7.
changes: Plans change costs, covered drugs and networks every year. Changes made now take effect January 1, 2027.
Start with the Annual Notice of Change your parent's plan mailed this fall. It lists what's different.
Are all their prescriptions still covered, and at what cost? Are their doctors and pharmacy still in network?
Pushy sales calls ramp up now. Medicare won't call out of the blue to sell a plan. Hang up and call 1-800-MEDICARE.
verdict_text: Anyone with Medicare can switch plans until December 7. People already in Medicare Advantage get another chance to switch January 1 to March 31.

headline: Recall: about 338,800 DREO space heaters
subhead: They can overheat and catch fire.
changes: Model DR-HSH015: a black ceramic heater, about 11.5 inches wide by 13 inches tall, with a remote.
Only units made April 2025 through January 2026. Check the label underneath for date codes 2025/04 to 2026/01.
Sold at Costco and online at Dreo.com, Best Buy, Kohl's, Lowe's, QVC, Home Depot and others, $70 to $110.
DREO received 17 reports of the heaters igniting, including 3 with property damage and 1 burn injury.
verdict_text: Stop using a recalled heater now. DREO offers a free replacement: you'll be asked to unplug it, cut the cord and send a photo.

headline: Home for Thanksgiving? Notice gently.
subhead: A visit can make slow changes easier to spot.
changes: Around the house: little or expired food, unopened mail or unpaid bills, more clutter, missed or mixed-up medications.
Health and getting around: noticeable weight change, falls or trouble walking, clothes that don't suit the weather.
Memory and mood: memory slips that disrupt daily life, trouble with familiar tasks, confusion about the day, mood changes.
These can have other causes, like depression, infection or medications. A doctor's visit is the right first step.
One sign isn't a verdict. Jot down what you noticed and compare notes with siblings after the holiday, not at the table.
Start small: pick a quiet moment, ask instead of accuse, and offer one practical help, like grocery delivery or a ride.
verdict_text: Talking early, while your parent can help decide, keeps more options open: help at home, adult day, respite care or assisted living.
actions: Save this for the drive home

headline: Par Health recalls Brevital Sodium injection vials
subhead: Particulate matter found inside 500 mg vials
changes: Product: Brevital Sodium (Methohexital Sodium) For Injection, USP, 500 mg/vial
Reason for recall: presence of particulate matter identified as cellulose
20,567 vials affected; distributed US Nationwide and Canada
Recall classification: Class I; recall status is ongoing
verdict_text: Class I recall means this product may cause serious harm. Healthcare providers and facilities holding this product should act immediately.
actions: Do not use any vials of Brevital Sodium from this recall.
Contact your healthcare provider or pharmacist before making any treatment changes.
Healthcare facilities should quarantine and return affected vials per Par Pharmaceutical guidance.

headline: UMARY Hyaluronic Acid capsules recalled nationwide
subhead: Hidden prescription drugs found inside supplement capsules
changes: Product contains undeclared Dexamethasone, a prescription steroid
Undeclared Diclofenac, a prescription anti-inflammatory, also found
Undeclared Omeprazole, a prescription stomach drug, also found
Marketed without an FDA-approved application; recall is ongoing
verdict_text: Anyone using this supplement should stop immediately. Hidden prescription drugs can cause serious harm, especially for older adults.
actions: Stop using UMARY Acido Hialuronico 850mg capsules immediately
Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before stopping any related treatment
Contact IBeautiStore.com or your retailer about returning the product

headline: NJ state of emergency: Thanksgiving storm
subhead: How to keep an older parent safe through Thursday's nor'easter.
changes: The statewide state of emergency starts at 6 p.m. tonight. The worst conditions come on Thanksgiving Day, improving Friday.
Expect wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph, 1 to 3 inches of rain, and likely power outages. Travel isn't banned, but officials urge staying off the roads.
Visiting Mom or Dad? Get there tonight or stay home Thursday. A video call beats a crash. Never drive through a flooded road.
Tonight: charge phones and medical devices, gather a week of medications and a med list, and put flashlights (not candles) by the bed.
Oxygen, CPAP or other powered equipment? Check backup batteries and tanks, and decide where your parent goes if the power stays out.
If the power goes out: never run a generator, grill or gas stove indoors or in a garage. Stay 30 feet from downed wires. Keep the fridge closed.
verdict_text: Older adults who live alone or rely on powered medical equipment are most at risk when the lights go out. A plan made tonight beats one made in the dark.
actions: Call a parent who lives alone Thursday AM and PM

headline: Traveling with Mom or Dad this season?
subhead: A little planning makes the trip easier for everyone.
changes: Book nonstop flights when you can, travel at your parent's best time of day, and leave room for rest.
Carry-on, not checked: medications in labeled bottles plus extra days, a medication list, and insurance cards.
Call the airline ahead to request a wheelchair or boarding help. At the airport, ask any TSA officer for a Passenger Support Specialist.
On long trips, get up and move often and drink water. Ask the doctor about compression stockings.
If memory is a concern, keep routines familiar and make sure your parent carries ID and an emergency contact.
When you arrive: check for loose rugs and cords, and add a night-light on the path to the bathroom.
verdict_text: Original Medicare covers care anywhere in the U.S. Medicare Advantage plans may limit out-of-network care, so call the plan before an out-of-state trip.
actions: At the airport: ask TSA for a Passenger Support Specialist

headline: Stay NJ's income limit is now $200,000
subhead: What senior homeowners should know before 2027 payments.
changes: The state budget signed June 30, 2026 cut the Stay NJ income limit from $500,000 to $200,000. Payments in 2027 go only to households at or under $200,000.

2027 maximum benefit, per year: up to $100,000 income, $6,500. $100,000 to $150,000, $5,000. $150,000 to $200,000, $4,000. Over $200,000, $0. The state says these assume no Stay NJ changes in the FY2028 budget.
Who qualifies: you or your spouse were 65 or older during 2025, you owned and lived in the home all of 2025, and the home is subject to property taxes (or P.I.L.O.T.).
Renters and mobile home owners are not eligible. Social Security disability under 65 doesn't qualify you on its own, but a married couple can qualify if one spouse is 65 or older.
verdict_text: If your parent's household income is over $200,000, they shouldn't count on a Stay NJ payment in 2027. The 2025 benefit is paid in February and May 2027.
actions: Each applicant gets a statement with their Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ amounts

headline: Medicare negotiated drug list updated November 2026
subhead: New deselections and 2028 price facts added
changes: New fact sheet and infographic published for negotiated prices taking effect in 2028
By March 1, 2027, CMS will post a price explanation for each drug with an agreed price for 2028
Five more drugs deselected: Farxiga, Januvia, Janumet/Janumet XR, Ofev, and Pomalyst removed January 1, 2028
Xeljanz/Xeljanz XR and Xolair deselected with removal effective January 1, 2029
verdict_text: People on Medicare Part D or Part B who take these drugs should check whether negotiated prices still apply to their medication.
actions: Check if your drug is on the updated negotiated price list at Medicare.gov
Ask your pharmacist whether your drug's negotiated price still applies in 2027 or 2028
Call 1-800-MEDICARE or NJ SHIP at 1-800-792-8820 with coverage questions

categories.explanation: Multiple drugs are being removed from the Medicare negotiated price program, meaning the lower Maximum Fair Price will no longer apply to those medications after their removal dates.

headline: Get free, unbiased Medicare help in North Jersey
subhead: A trained counselor costs nothing and sells nothing.
changes: Ask to be connected to your county SHIP office in Bergen, Essex, Hudson, Morris, Passaic, Sussex, Union, or Warren.
Schedule a free, confidential appointment by phone, virtually, or in person at your county office.
At your session, ask about Medicare plans, Medigap, Part D, claims denials, and programs that cut your costs.
verdict_text: SHIP counselors are trained volunteers who give free, unbiased help and never sell insurance, so your family gets clear answers with no pressure.
actions: Ask: What drug plan or Medigap fits my parent's needs and budget?

headline: Caring for someone in New Jersey? Start here.
subhead: You don't have to figure out every service on your own.
changes: New Jersey's new Caregiver Support Hub puts resources, training and support information in one place.
Visit caregiver.nj.gov to find help for the person you care for, and for yourself.
Or call 877-222-3737. It connects you to your county's Aging & Disability Resource Connection.
Helping a parent with rides, meals, bills or medications? You're a caregiver, and this is for you.
verdict_text: Caregivers often spend hours finding the right office. One website and one phone number point you to what your county offers.
actions: Save this or share it with a caregiver

headline: NJ caregiver hub now live & Part B rises to $209.40 in 2027
subhead: 4 stories for families you may have missed
changes: NJ Human Services launched caregiver.nj.gov with more than 350 resources for the state's 1.1 million family caregivers.
CMS set the 2027 Medicare Part B standard premium at $209.40/month, up $6.50, and the annual deductible at $292.
FTC warned older adults: scammers use AI voice cloning to impersonate grandchildren in distress.
FTC warned that scammers are using three new tactics to steal VA disability benefits from veterans and older adults.
verdict_text: This week brings a new tool and important numbers: New Jersey opened a one-stop caregiver resource hub, and federal agencies updated the costs and fraud risks every older adult should know heading into 2027.
actions: Book a free Medicare review with NJ SHIP: 1-800-792-8820
Check the pantry and medicine cabinet against this week's recalls
Look up a parent's nursing home on Medicare.gov Care Compare
source_doc: NJ Care Compass weekly recap for Nov 16–22, 2026

headline: Look up any nursing home before you visit
subhead: Four checks that take under ten minutes.
changes: Check the 1-to-5 star rating: it combines health inspections, staffing, and quality measures in one score.
Read the last three years of health inspection reports to see citations, what was wrong, and whether it was fixed.
Check staffing: look for nurse hours per resident per day and staff turnover — more hours, less turnover is better.
Look for any Medicare penalties — a fine or denied payment — listed on the facility's Care Compare page.
verdict_text: A quick Care Compare search before you visit can reveal inspection citations, low staffing, or Medicare penalties that a tour alone will not show.
actions: Search any NJ nursing home free at medicare.gov/care-compare
Call NJ Long-Term Care Ombudsman: 1-877-582-6995 (all NJ counties)
File a care complaint with NJ Dept. of Health: 1-800-792-9770
